source.title: Flatness-Aware Prompt Selection Improves Accuracy and Sample Efficiency
source.authors: Lingfeng Shen; Weiting Tan; Boyuan Zheng; Daniel Khashabi

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports experiments on whether flatness measures or flatness-aware prompt selection track or improve downstream performance for pretrained language models and continuous prompts. This is a related setting to the catalog’s flatness/generalization version, but it does not test that version’s trained-network generalization-gap comparison.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s own reported flatness or flatness-aware results. Generalization and sharpness results cited from prior work are not rows. Flatness values themselves are not reported as outcomes; prompt-selection comparisons and accuracy results are.
record.test_reason: The study uses flatness to build prompt-selection and prefix-tuning methods and evaluates their downstream performance. It does not test V7's relationship between magnitude-aware sharpness and train–test gaps among comparably fitted convolutional networks, or any other listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: combining prompt flatness with existing selection metrics improves prompt selection, and SAM-based prefix-tuning improves accuracy on the three tested classification tasks. The authors also report improved sample efficiency.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a prompt-parameter flatness metric for selecting prompts and applies SAM to prefix-tuning. It does not compare trained networks’ generalization gaps or use the magnitude-aware perturbation measure described in V7.
record.method_sensitivity: For P_Flat estimation, the paper reports sensitivity to perturbation size and sample count: it says the optimal perturbation size is around 1e-4 in §4.4, while Figure 6’s caption says around 1e-5 for SEN+P_Flat; it also says performance degrades as perturbation size increases. It reports that combining flatness with MI or SEN generally outperforms flatness alone. These are prompt-selection findings, not measurements of training–test gap.

fits_no_version.finding: Combining P_FLAT with MI or sensitivity generally improves prompt-selection correlations and selected-prompt performance; flatness alone is generally less effective.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter-perturbation sensitivity can complement existing metrics for selecting accurate prompts for pretrained language models.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM prefix-tuning improves GPT2-medium classification accuracy by 0.6, 0.9, and 0.8 percentage points on SST-2, AGNews, and SNLI, respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharpness-aware prefix-tuning can improve downstream classification accuracy relative to Adam in these settings.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (Findings), 2023
record.problems: The experiments assess prompt-selection metrics and downstream task performance, rather than trained-network generalization gaps. The empirical tasks are classification tasks; the paper says generation tasks remain for future work. The paper also notes its method requires a small labeled development set to adjust alpha.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version row is extracted for the main discrete-prompt retrieval and correlation experiments: these report prompt-selection performance or correlation with test accuracy, not a measure of the training–test gap named in V7. The prefix-tuning task-level accuracy comparisons are kept as R1–R3 because they report a flatness-aware intervention and downstream outcome.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance under random versus natural labels.
Test error as width increases beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under specified tuning budgets; SAM versus Adam does not provide this comparison.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance versus train–test gaps among comparably fitted convolutional networks, including ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: P_FLAT perturbs pretrained LLM weights conditional on a prompt; it is not simply a prompt-parameter flatness measure. Its Gaussian perturbations are not scaled to weight magnitudes. The omitted discrete-prompt experiments are declared in rows_left_out and do not supply missing evidence for V7.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test accuracy.
Network width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.

The paper tests whether flatness relates to downstream accuracy in prompt selection, but does not report the trained networks’ train–test gaps or compare magnitude-aware sharpness against the measures named in V7.

rows.subject: GPT2-medium
rows.operation_detail: Prefix-tuning with flatness-aware optimization using SAM
rows.note: The paper reports an accuracy gain for its flatness-aware prefix-tuning setup; it does not measure a training–test gap.
rows.check: Table 1 correctly reports SST-2 accuracy increasing from 92.5 (0.1) to 93.1 (0.1). This is SAM versus Adam prefix-tuning performance, not a measurement of magnitude-aware sharpness or its association with generalization gaps. Exclude as a claim-result row.
